newsitem.title: DUBAI: Second Iraqi oil tanker leaves Mina al-Bakr.
newsitem.headline: Second Iraqi oil tanker leaves Mina al-Bakr.

text.p: The second Iraqi oil tanker from the Middle East Gulf under the United Nations "oil-for-food" deal left the Mina al-Bakr export terminal on Thursday, Gulf shipping sources said on Thursday.
The 272,000 deadweight tonne Leonidas tanker, chartered by American independent oil trader Bayoil, left the terminal at 1100 local time (0600 GMT), they said.
Leonidas followed on from the Star Africa, chartered by U.S. Coastal Corp, which left for the Caribbean island of Aruba on Tuesday.
The destination of the Leonidas, the first cargo under Bayoil's six-month 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) with Baghdad's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO), was not immediately known.
Leonidas is scheduled to return to al-Bakr next month.

The U.N. has confirmed that it has so far approved 13 contracts under the "oil-for-food" deal under which Iraq is allowed to export $2 billion of its oil over six month in return for humanitarian supplies.
Iraq's first crude tanker export was from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Monday.
The "larger share" of exports from the deal will come from the port of Ceyhan.
Gulf industry sources on Thursday said that eight of the first 10 contracts approved by the U.N. would leave the Turkish export terminal at Ceyhan.
